purpose: Qualify Dropbox CAS transport at production-like object size after successful cross-chat canary.
root_cause: The currently exposed Dropbox connector has no byte-preserving local-file upload or upload-session action and create_file accepts only an inline UTF-8 JSON string (max 5 MB). The orchestration surface provides no deterministic binding from runtime-generated bytes/local files into that content parameter. Therefore an empirical production-size write/readback cannot be executed without re-emitting multi-megabyte payload content through the model/tool-argument channel, which is not a valid deterministic artifact transport path for QROS.

evidence.dropbox_binary_tool_search: Only create_file matched; its contract explicitly says text inline only and to use a byte-preserving flow for binary, but no such upload action is exposed.

architecture_validity: CAS_MANIFEST_HASH_ORDINAL_READBACK_PROTOCOL_REMAINS_VALID; ONLY HEAVY WRITE BACKEND IS UNQUALIFIED
next_legitimate_action: Select or expose a byte-preserving persistent writer that accepts a local file/connector-file reference or upload session; rerun identical 4x2MiB qualification unchanged. Until then use deterministic rematerialization for resumability-critical heavy derivatives and retain Dropbox CAS only for payload sizes that are actually written/readback verified.
